name: avd-hostpool
description: A pooled host pool, desktop application group, workspace, and autoscaling plan with diagnostics - the control plane for secure, cost-managed remote desktops.
what: The Azure Virtual Desktop control plane: a pooled host pool (breadth-first load balancing, start-VM-on-connect, hardened RDP properties that block clipboard/printer/drive redirection), a Desktop application group, a workspace exposing it to users, and an optional autoscaling plan that ramps capacity up for business hours and stops idle hosts off-peak. Host pool diagnostics flow to Log Analytics.
why: Organizations need secure, centrally governed remote desktops for contractors, BYOD, regulated data access, and burst workforces - without shipping data to endpoints. This establishes the AVD control plane and autoscaling so session hosts can be joined into a governed, observable, cost-managed pool.
potentialUseCases: Secure remote access for contractors and third parties
Regulated data access where data must stay in Azure
Seasonal or burst workforce desktop provisioning
BYOD / unmanaged-device access to corporate apps

reliability: Pooled host pool with breadth-first load balancing across hosts
Workspace + app group decoupled from session host lifecycle
security: Hardened RDP properties block clipboard, printer, and drive redirection
Data stays in Azure; endpoints receive pixels only
Host pool audit logs to Log Analytics
costOptimization: Autoscaling plan ramps hosts for business hours and stops idle hosts off-peak
Start-VM-on-connect avoids paying for unused hosts
Scaling plan disabled in dev to keep costs minimal
operationalExcellence: Host pool diagnostics and connection logs centralized in Log Analytics
Control plane defined as code and versioned
performanceEfficiency: Session limit tuned per host to balance density and experience
Breadth-first balancing spreads load during peak

cost.profile: AVD control plane is free; cost is driven by the session host VMs you join (priced separately). Prod profile assumes an autoscaling pool of session hosts.

components.name: Session host VMs (D-series, example)
components.notes: Example: 2 hosts averaged over business hours with autoscaling. Replace with your pool sizing.

components.name: Session host managed disks (Premium SSD)
components.notes: One OS disk per session host.
